name: local_losses_idelchik_elbows
title: Local pressure loss of curved bends: Idelchik coefficients, single-phase and two-phase (function library)
summary: EES FUNCTION library of the loss coefficient of circular pipe bends (Idelchik coefficients as in LaboThapPy): angle coefficient A1, radius coefficients A2 and B1, laminar/intermediate/high-Reynolds branches blended with a cubic step, roughness correction from the friction of the bend arc, total coefficient zeta_tot and pressure drop zeta_tot*rho*v^2/2, with a two-phase extension through a mixture density (the fixed upstream in-situ formula alpha*rho_v+(1-alpha)*rho_l); a mode argument gives the blending as written in the source (whose stepsmoother calls look argument-swapped) or with the arguments reordered.

authors: I. E. Idelchik (Handbook of Hydraulic Resistance, 1986)
P. K. Swamee and A. K. Jain (Swamee-Jain friction factor, 1976)

origin.notes: LaboThapPy commit f03f7f47 (local clone ~/git/LaboThapPy): curved_elbow.py (compute_re_lam_transition, compute_idelchik_coefficients, compute_reynolds_correction_turbulent, compute_zeta_LOC, compute_cf_fri, compute_zeta_tot, pressure_drop_curved_elbow), helpers toolbox/helper_function/step_smoother.py and correlations/pressure_drop/pipe_DP.py (friction_factor_swamee_jain). curved_elbow.py is byte-identical on branch origin/Elise at 9364dfc6; the two-phase density follows the fixed upstream compute_two_phase_density of correlations/properties/two_phase.py (commits 3977f2b0/44de58bd), adapted 2026-11-02 (see README). The source is a port of the Modelica Dissipation library CurvedBend_LDP (Idelchik; Miller; VDI-Waermeatlas Lac 6). Translation published under the CoolSolve_Library MIT license (decision D3). Model adapted 2026-11-02 to the upstream density fix.
